data.body:
Cite re-measurement against origin/main e2ed08b343a (2026-10-28), by whole-tree per-symbol sweep rather than sampling. The description has been rewritten with corrected cites; this comment corrects the FIRST comment's test lists, which cannot be edited in place. It supersedes the second comment (whose basis 360d504f5ceb is 290 commits stale).

SUBSTANTIVE GAPS the citation fixes alone would not have caught. The plan as written could not pass its own AC1, on four hits, two of which its prose explicitly protected:
1. `src/rebar/llm/evals/provider_parity.py:80` `AGENTIC_SOLVERS` contains `"ticket-quality"`. The old Scope declared it OUT of scope ("the eval-harness epic replaces it; harmless until run"), but AC1 greps `src`, so AC1 could never have passed. Now pulled IN scope (step 7).
2. `docs/llm-framework.md:692` names `aggregate_findings` in the b744 retirement history. The old step 6 said it "stays as history", but AC1 excludes only release-notes, adr and experiments, so `docs/llm-framework.md` is in scope and AC1 could never have passed. Now the sentence keeps the history and drops the dead symbol name (step 7).
3. `src/rebar/llm/prompting/prompts.py:153` uses `ticket_quality.md` → `ticket-quality` as its id-normalization example. Unhandled by the old plan; AC1 would have failed. Now swapped to `code_quality.md` → `code-quality`, matching the identical fix already planned for `docs/reuse-surface.md`.
4. `tests/unit/test_new_eval_specs.py:2` names ticket-quality in its module docstring. The old plan touched only the `:15` golden tuple. Now both.

MISSING IMPLEMENTATION STEP: `tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py:532` asserts `len(_EXPECTED_RUN_REQUEST_SITES) == 21`. Deleting the `_review_ticket_impl` row at `:486` makes it 20, so the constant must change or `make verify` fails. Added to Testing.

FIRST-COMMENT LINE CORRECTIONS (old -> new). Delete tests: `test_review_ops_characterization.py:28,45` -> `:23,:40` (`test_review_ticket_contract`, `test_review_ticket_graph_target_kind`); `test_review_as_workflow.py:47,59` -> `:45,:57`, and the kept bridge test `:23` -> `:21`; `test_subcall_class_selection.py:178-200` -> `:102-122`, registry rows `:346-355` -> `:247-257`, `:594` -> `:486`. Rewrites: `test_gate_source_threading.py:95,117,143` -> `:94,:119,:145`; `test_attested_signing.py:206` -> `:209`; `test_snapshot_environments.py` ~`:105` -> `:107`; `test_llm_framework.py:73-86` -> parametrize `:75-80`, def `:83`; `test_eval_solver.py:182,204` -> `:181,:203`. Swaps: `test_pydantic_ai_cutover_live.py:207` -> `:181`; `test_execution_mode.py:26-224` -> `:26-185`.

UNCHANGED on the tip (verified, not assumed): `test_llm_framework.py:43`, `:438-515`, `:682`, `:714`, `:770`, `:783`; `test_eval_solver.py:47,57`; `test_review_ops_characterization.py:73`; `test_review_output_budget.py:414` (the second comment's correction still holds; the engine call is at `:428`); `test_review_skeleton.py:104,:117` (likewise); golden sets `test_new_eval_specs.py:15`, `test_prompt_cache_split.py:32`, `test_prompt_front_matter.py:183`; `test_generated_surface_markers.py:130`; `test_agent_op_safeguard.py:86`; `test_prompt_index.py:17-36`, `test_prompt_variants.py:14-110`, `test_prompts_git_canonical.py:18-57`, `test_prompt_library_writes.py:48-109`.

ITEMS NOW MOOT — do not re-litigate:
- The editor epic HAS landed. `tests/unit/workflow/test_prompt_authoring.py`, `test_editor_batch.py` and `tests/e2e/` no longer exist, so the first comment's conditional ("if that epic has not landed first, apply the same swap there") resolves to no action.
- `tests/unit/workflow/test_prompt_refs.py:12` no longer contains `ticket-quality`; it is now a comment about supplied template variables. The planned swap there is a no-op.
- `tests/external/test_llm_trace.py:128,132` and `tests/unit/test_code_review_gate_session.py:2` have zero hits for the id. Already clean.
- "the three `aggregate_findings` tests" in `test_llm_framework.py:438-515` is TWO test functions (`:438`, `:473`); the third call site at `:515` is inside the second test.
- `_VERIFY_MIN_STEPS` does not exist. `test_completion_budget.py` covers the completion floor as `verify_step_floor` / `_VERIFY_STEP_FLOOR_MAX`; the substance of the coverage claim holds, only the constant name was wrong.

OTHER DESCRIPTION CITES CORRECTED: `operations.py:135-201` -> `:135-218` (runs to EOF); the `_REVIEW_MIN_STEPS` deletion range `:38-42` -> `:35-42` (deleting only `:38-42` would have orphaned three comment lines); `default_reviewer_id:45-55` -> `:45-54`; `review_workflows.py:86` -> def at `:70`, engine call at `:86`; `test_review_as_workflow.py:16` -> `:14`; `review_skeleton.yaml:39` -> `:31` (and `code-quality` `:37` -> `:29`, `completion-verifier` `:51` -> `:42`; the claimed `:10` comment mentioning the id does not exist); `prompts.py:290-293` -> `:291`; `__init__.py:60` -> `:59` (plus `__all__` `:127`); `__init__.py:107` -> `:106`; `release-notes.md:532` -> `:946`; `llm-framework.md:395-397` -> `:399`, `:352` -> `:355`, `:662` -> `:692`; `reuse-surface.md:313` -> `:311`; `code-review.yaml:105-148` -> `:71-108,126-148`; `provider_parity.py:88` -> `:80`; `gate_ops.py:191` -> `:192`.

TWO DESCRIPTION CLAIMS WERE WRONG, not merely drifted, and have been rewritten:
- `src/rebar/_deprecations.py:109-111` does not record any decision about the review engine. That range is unrelated `RemovedInput.__post_init__` validation, and the file contains no reference to the review surfaces at all. The citation is removed.
- `tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json:2321` was cited as the guarded public entry for `select_reviewers`. The baseline entry is at `:2306` and belongs to `rebar.llm.prompting.prompts`, not the `rebar.llm` facade; `rebar.llm` is absent from `gen_api_surface.py:54-62 MODULES`. Consequence: removing the `aggregate_findings` export does not touch the API surface at all, so AC6's `gen_api_surface.py --check` passes trivially rather than guarding this change. Stated accurately now.

VERIFIED STILL TRUE: AC5's workflow-untouched grep returns zero hits on the tip; `aggregate.py` is 125 LOC; `spec_scan.py:13,137`; ADR 0108 `:123`; `workflow_ops.py:24,150`; `docs/workflow-engine.md:103`; `docs/api-stability.md:28`; `eval_solver.py:406-414` exactly; `index.json:80` with the sole `"default": true` at `:84`; `operations.py` docstring `:1-17` and `__all__:33`; `prompts.py:620`; `test_prompt_index.py::test_index_has_exactly_one_default` at `:67`; `test_review_budget.py` is 80 lines with exactly 2 tests; `assemble_context` has a genuine live consumer at `workflow/gate_ops.py:192` (import at `:179`), so it correctly stays.

ONE NOTE FOR THE IMPLEMENTER on an adjacent fact the old plan got subtly wrong: `code_quality.md` has NO `applies_to` key in its front matter; `applies_to: []` appears in the generated `index.json` for BOTH prompts. So "today `applies_to: []` means it is never selected" was not the reason `code-quality` is unselected — `ticket-quality` has the same empty `applies_to` and IS selected, via `default: true`. The action (flip `default`) is unchanged and correct; only the stated reason was wrong, and the description now says so accurately.
